cards.title: Respecting ROKAF Rank
cards.body: ROKAF follows a strict hierarchy. Address superiors by their rank and last name. Avoid using first names or informal language. Understand that rank influences decision-making and communication.
doThis: Use formal titles and last names

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: South Korea (2025)

cards.title: Navigating Checkpoints
cards.body: Checkpoints are common. Carry proper identification and follow instructions. Be patient and polite. Understand that security staff may not speak English fluently.

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: South Korea (2025)

cards.title: Respecting Hierarchy in Meals
cards.body: In South Korea, seniors eat first. Wait for elders to start before you begin eating. Use chopsticks to serve yourself from shared dishes, but don't put them in your mouth directly from the communal bowl. Avoid sticking chopsticks vertically into food, as this is a funeral rite.
doThis: Wait for seniors to start eating first.
Use chopsticks to serve yourself from shared dishes.
avoidThis: Put chopsticks in your mouth directly from communal bowls.

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: South Korea (2025)

cards.title: Polite Refusal of Food
cards.body: When offered more food, initially decline as a polite gesture. If you want more, accept on the second or third offer. This custom helps maintain harmony and respect during meals. Loud slurping is normal and a sign of enjoying the food.
doThis: Initially decline extra food as a polite gesture.
Accept more food on the second or third offer if desired.
avoidThis: Accept extra food immediately without initial refusal.
Criticize or comment on the loud slurping.

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: South Korea (2025)

cards.title: Respecting Hierarchy in Refusal
cards.body: In South Korea, hierarchy is crucial. When refusing, address seniors with respect. Use titles and indirect language to maintain harmony.
doThis: Use titles like 'nim' or 'sangsaengnim' for seniors
Be indirect; say 'It's difficult' instead of 'No'
avoidThis: Use first names for elders or superiors

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: South Korea (2025)

cards.title: Saving Face in Refusal
cards.body: South Koreans value 'saving face'. Avoid public criticism. Use polite, indirect language when refusing to maintain respect.
doThis: Use indirect language; say 'Let's consider' instead of 'No'

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: South Korea (2025)

cards.title: Respecting Hierarchy in Korea
cards.body: Korean culture values hierarchy and respect. Address seniors with their titles and use formal language. Avoid direct disagreement to maintain harmony.
doThis: Use titles and formal language with seniors
Ask open-ended questions instead of direct disagreement
avoidThis: Use first names for elders or superiors
Criticize publicly or openly disagree with seniors

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: South Korea (2025)

cards.title: Saving Face in Korea
cards.body: Avoid public criticism and indirect communication to save face. Use polite language and consider the feelings of others to maintain social harmony.
doThis: Use indirect communication for sensitive topics

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: South Korea (2025)

cards.title: Respecting Hierarchy in S. Korea
cards.body: South Koreans value hierarchy. Address seniors with their title and last name. Avoid direct disagreement. Be mindful of criticism to save face.

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: South Korea (2025)

cards.title: Navigating Checkpoints in S. Korea
cards.body: Checkpoints are common. Carry ID at all times. Be polite and patient with security staff. Follow instructions carefully.

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: South Korea (2025)

cards.title: Addressing Seniors in Korea
cards.body: South Korea's hierarchy is important. Use titles and last names for seniors. Women hold power at home but may have lower work positions. Men often avoid domestic tasks.
doThis: Use titles and last names for seniors

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: South Korea (2025)

cards.title: Gender Roles in Korean Work
cards.body: Women often juggle work and domestic duties. Long workdays and social activities can make balancing both roles difficult. Some women delay marriage or leave work until children are grown.
avoidThis: Assume domestic duties are only women's
Ignore career challenges faced by women

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: South Korea (2025)

cards.title: Religious Diversity in South Korea
cards.body: South Korea is religiously diverse, with Christianity and Buddhism being the most common. Many locals blend traditions. Respect all beliefs and avoid religious debates. Observe holidays like Christmas and Buddha's birthday.

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: South Korea (2025)

cards.title: Indigenous Beliefs and Practices
cards.body: Many South Koreans blend indigenous beliefs like shamanism with their primary religion. Shamans perform rituals to communicate with spirits. Respect these practices and avoid interference.

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: South Korea (2025)

cards.title: Gift Giving: Hierarchy Matters
cards.body: Gifts show respect for hierarchy. Give gifts to seniors first. Use both hands when presenting or receiving gifts. Gifts are usually refused once or twice before being accepted. Avoid giving gifts that are too expensive or too personal.
doThis: Use both hands when presenting/receiving gifts
Refuse a gift once or twice before accepting

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: South Korea (2025)

cards.title: Gift Giving: Save Face
cards.body: Criticism and disagreement should be handled delicately to save face. Use indirect language and suggest alternatives. Avoid public criticism or blunt disagreement. Refusals should be polite and considerate.
doThis: Suggest alternatives instead of outright disagreement
Be polite and considerate when refusing

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: South Korea (2025)

cards.title: Respecting Hierarchy at Meals
cards.body: South Koreans value hierarchy. Wait for seniors to start eating. Use chopsticks to serve yourself from communal dishes, not to eat directly. Avoid sticking chopsticks upright in food. Accept food offers politely, even if you don't want more.
doThis: Wait for seniors to begin eating.
Use chopsticks to serve yourself from shared dishes.
avoidThis: Eat directly from communal dishes with chopsticks.

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: South Korea (2025)

cards.title: Navigating Checkpoints and Security
cards.body: Checkpoints are common. Carry ID at all times. South Koreans may be curious about foreigners. Security staff may ask questions. Be patient and polite. Do not argue or show frustration. Always follow instructions.
doThis: Be patient and polite with security staff.

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: South Korea (2025)

cards.title: Respect Hierarchy in Meetings
cards.body: South Korean meetings emphasize seniority. Address seniors formally using their title and last name. Wait for seniors to initiate conversation and follow their lead. Disagreements should be handled delicately to maintain harmony.

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: South Korea (2025)

cards.title: Navigating Checkpoints and Security
cards.body: Checkpoints and security staff are common on base. Carry proper identification at all times. Be patient and polite when interacting with security staff and local nationals. Follow instructions carefully to avoid delays.

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: South Korea (2025)

cards.title: Respecting Rank on Radio
cards.body: South Koreans value hierarchy. Use titles and last names for seniors. Be polite and indirect. Avoid public criticism or disagreement. Save face by being tactful.
doThis: Use titles and last names for seniors

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: South Korea (2025)

cards.title: Radio Etiquette in South Korea
cards.body: Speak clearly and politely. Use formal titles. Avoid sarcasm. Laughing may not mean amusement. Be mindful of volume and intonation.
doThis: Be mindful of volume and intonation

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: South Korea (2025)

cards.title: Respecting Hierarchy in ROKAF
cards.body: South Korean military culture values hierarchy. Address superiors with their rank and last name. Avoid direct disagreement or criticism in public. Use indirect language when necessary.
doThis: Use formal titles and last names for superiors

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: South Korea (2025)

cards.title: Navigating Base Checkpoints
cards.body: Checkpoints are common. Carry ID at all times. Be patient and polite with security staff. Local nationals may need escorts. Follow instructions carefully.
